output.name: Thelan
output.myth: Ennu the Kite-Wright made a gull once, of sailcloth and goose-bone, and gave it to a girl on the windward cliff who had asked the wind a question and got no answer. The gull flew well. It climbed past the goats and nesting ledges until it hung over the sea. Then Tavo came along the cliff laughing, as he does, and took one wing in his teeth and tore it. The gull hung there, wobbling. Aun saw it from the Lamp Road and wanted to know how far it would go, so he cut the string with his knife. Now the gull lies up in the north, in sight of the Fid, whose rope frayed at the ends. Its tail still trails toward the islands like a rope nobody pulled. From there it watches the Child's Kite to the west, the little boat Tavo took past the rocks, and knows what it is to have one wing. The girl still looks up when the wind goes round to the north. Hesk keeps count of the string she lost, and says nothing.
output.finding: Find the Child's Kite, then look a fist and a half due east of it, where the Tethered Gull hangs in the north with its tail trailing toward the islands.
